description: Align coder-agent skills and user docs to the real mo CLI/API command surface (text-only change): epic skill autopilot lifecycle, dispatcher complete command surface, CLI reference missing groups, display-vs-functional-entry convention, and skill cache sync.

tasks.title: Record display-surface vs functional-entry boundary convention
tasks.description: Add a new section to design/conventions.md recording the standing three-tier boundary rule from design.md Decision 4: (1) display/read-only surfaces stay Web-only with no CLI/skill entry; (2) state-changing functional entry points get a mo CLI command; (3) a coder-agent skill entry is added only when there is methodology to encode (multi-step flow, templates, decisions, confirmation gates), not for every CLI command. Frame it as the standing test for future 'should this get a CLI/skill entry?' questions.
acceptanceCriteria: design/conventions.md contains a new section titled to reflect the display-surface vs functional-entry boundary.
The section records all three tiers (Web-only display; CLI for state-changing entry; skill only when methodology exists).
The rule is framed as the standing test for CLI/skill scope decisions, not as epic-specific commentary.
grep -i 'web.*only\|display' design/conventions.md returns the new rule; no other design file (e.g. architecture.md) is modified for this rule.
tasks.output: design/conventions.md with the new display-vs-functional-entry boundary section
tasks.notes: This convention durably records the rule that justifies the operations-skill decision (Decision 1): operations satisfy tier 2 (CLI) but not tier 3 (no methodology), so they stay in the dispatcher rather than becoming a dedicated mohist-operate skill.

tasks.title: Rewrite epic skill to autopilot-first lifecycle and remove stale framing
tasks.description: Rewrite the lifecycle section of packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/skill-data/mohist-create-epic/SKILL.md from 'done/close only' to an autopilot-first model: recommend mo epic start as the default way to drive an epic, document mo epic start/pause/resume with idempotency and the running-but-idle state, then keep done/close as the terminal tail. Remove the sentence claiming the epic does not participate in workflow execution (currently at the 'Epic shape' intro). Source the lifecycle content from docs/epics.md and keep the two consistent. Also refresh the front-matter description and the end-to-end checklist to mention autopilot.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/skill-data/mohist-create-epic/SKILL.md documents mo epic start, mo epic pause, and mo epic resume with their effects on autonomous issue progression.
The skill documents the idempotency semantics of mo epic start (starting an already-running epic is a no-op) and the running-but-idle state (all member issues complete, awaiting the next).
The skill explicitly recommends autopilot self-directed progression over manually starting each member issue.
grep -i 'does not participate in workflow execution\|non-executing organizer' packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/skill-data/mohist-create-epic/SKILL.md returns no matches (stale framing removed).
The done/close terminal lifecycle is retained.
docs/epics.md autopilot section (Start/Pause/Resume, idempotency, running-but-idle) is verified current and consistent with the skill content; no re-authoring required.
tasks.output: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/skill-data/mohist-create-epic/SKILL.md with autopilot-first lifecycle and de-staled framing
tasks.notes: Create mechanics (description, link, prerequisites) stay unchanged; only the lifecycle section, the stale 'non-executing' sentence, the front-matter description, and the checklist need edits. Source truth: docs/epics.md lifecycle section.

tasks.title: Rewrite dispatcher skill with complete issue/epic lifecycle command surface
tasks.description: Replace the partial CLI cheat-sheet in packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/skill-data/mohist/SKILL.md (currently 'mo issue show|list|start|approve|close, mo epic show, mo workflow list, mo label list' plus the 'Promote to a scenario skill' caveat) with the complete issue and epic lifecycle command surface. Issue lifecycle must include start, approve, reject, retry, rerun, stop, force-stop, resume, rebase, and close. Epic autopilot must include mo epic start, mo epic pause, and mo epic resume. This embodies the operations-skill decision (design.md Decision 1: keep operations in the dispatcher, do NOT create a mohist-operate skill) by making the dispatcher the single source for these lifecycle commands.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/skill-data/mohist/SKILL.md CLI command guidance documents the complete issue lifecycle: start, approve, reject, retry, rerun, stop, force-stop, resume, rebase, and close.
The dispatcher skill documents mo epic start, mo epic pause, and mo epic resume.
The partial cheat-sheet (show|list|start|approve|close only) is replaced; the 'Promote to a scenario skill once a stable practice emerges' caveat is removed.
All referenced mo commands exist in the real CLI (cross-check against mo --help / mo <cmd> --help); no advertised command is invented.
No mohist-operate skill is created and no manifest.json entry for one is added (Decision 1 embodied); the dispatcher is the single source for issue/epic lifecycle commands.
tasks.output: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/skill-data/mohist/SKILL.md with the complete issue/epic lifecycle command surface
tasks.notes: The operations-skill decision is recorded in design.md Decision 1 and justified by the T-001 boundary convention (tier 3: no methodology -> no dedicated skill). This task embodies that decision in the dispatcher content. Every command reference must match the real CLI per the contract-bearing-surface requirement.

tasks.title: Complete CLI reference: document missing command groups and drop false claims
tasks.description: Edit docs/cli-reference.md to (a) add concise cheat-sheet sections for the four previously omitted command groups — mo agent (create, list/ls, show, update, delete, session list/show/transcript/launch/followup/cancel), mo label (list/ls, add, update, remove/rm), mo workflow (list/ls), and mo otel (query <sql>, status) — matching the existing Issue/Epic section style; and (b) replace the false '和 Web UI 功能等价' / '本文是完整命令参考' opening with an accurate, humble scope statement (entry point for scripting/automation; documents the command groups; see mo --help for the full tree). Point to mo <cmd> --help for full flag detail rather than authoring deep-doc pages.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/cli-reference.md contains documented sections for the agent, label, workflow, and otel command groups.
Each new section's documented subcommands match the real CLI surface (verify against mo agent --help, mo label --help, mo workflow --help, mo otel --help).
mo workflow list is documented as distinct from mo project workflow template/config (which stays under 项目管理).
grep -i 'web ui 功能等价\|功能等价\|完整命令参考\|完整参考' docs/cli-reference.md returns no matches (false equivalence and absolute-completeness claims removed).
The opening describes the CLI's own scope without claiming parity with or equivalence to the Web UI, and points to mo --help for the full command tree.
tasks.output: docs/cli-reference.md with agent/label/workflow/otel sections and a humble scope statement
tasks.notes: Per design.md Decisions 2 and 3: match existing section style, do not author new deep-doc pages, and do not re-assert absolute completeness (a standing absolute would re-drift). Subcommand surface is verified from mo --help in design.md.

tasks.title: Sync edited skills to managed cache and verify source-cache consistency
tasks.description: After the epic and dispatcher skill source edits (T-002, T-003) land, run mo skills sync to propagate the edited skill-data into the managed cache, then verify with mo skills get mohist and mo skills get mohist-create-epic that the cache output matches the edited SKILL.md source byte-for-byte (modulo sync formatting normalization). This is the acceptance gate for skill propagation, not a runtime behavior change.
acceptanceCriteria: mo skills sync is run after T-002 and T-003 are complete, with no errors.
mo skills get mohist output matches packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/skill-data/mohist/SKILL.md source content (modulo sync formatting normalization).
mo skills get mohist-create-epic output matches packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/skill-data/mohist-create-epic/SKILL.md source content (modulo sync formatting normalization).
The synced dispatcher cache content reflects the complete issue/epic lifecycle command surface and the synced epic cache content reflects the autopilot lifecycle.
tasks.output: Managed skill cache in sync with edited skill source; verified via mo skills get
tasks.notes: Run sync once after both skill edits are complete (syncing the whole skill-data tree at once avoids redundant runs and prevents parallel races on the managed cache). This satisfies the issue acceptance criterion: skill 编辑后通过 skills sync 反映到托管缓存，mo skills get 输出与源一致.
